name: LeoFinance
technique: Private key compromise; Unrestricted contract minting
classificationNote: Classified by TypeSafe jev-1.13.0 (confidence 0.92). Replaced keyword guess "signature-crypto".
rootCause: On October 11, 2020, an attacker used a compromised WLEO contract minting key to create unlimited tokens, draining $42,000 in ETH from the Uniswap liquidity pool. The breach stemmed from the use of a hot wallet private key with no minting limits or multisig. Rapid community action recovered some funds and prompted a refactor of WLEO architecture to remove arbitrary minting and strengthen key security. The WLEO mint contract's private key, stored in a hot wallet with single-signer control, was compromised, granting the attacker unlimited mint authority. The design lacked minting limits, multi-signature protection, or supply controls, allowing arbitrary…
